THE DEPLOYMENT SCRIPT REPORTED FAILURE ON A DEPLOYMENT THAT SUCCEEDED, and the defect was mine (OTH-2026-00018 wrote it, OTH-2026-00019 found and fixed it). Its step-5 smoke tests used `curl -I`. The upstream is GET-only and answers HEAD with 405 by design, so the primary 'HTTPS 200' check failed against a healthy site. Proven from the vhost's own access log, which records the script's probes from 51.68.226.211 at 20:01:52Z: HEAD / 405, three times. A second check was worse than wrong — it read Content-Type from the HEAD 405 response, which is also application/json, so it PASSED for entirely the wrong reason and would have false-greened a broken API. A third asserted POST /api/health returns 403 at the edge; it returns 405, because an exact-match nginx location beats a regex one and `location = /api/health` did not inherit the `limit_except` from `location ~ ^/api/`. FIXED: every probe is now a GET using `-D- -o /dev/null` so the checks read the headers users actually get; the write-refusal property is asserted twice and separately — 403 at the edge on a regex-governed /api/ path, and 403-or-405 on /api/health — so neither can hide the other; and a redirect-target check was added. The template now repeats limit_except inside the exact-match block so future installs refuse writes uniformly at the edge. THE LIVE VHOST STILL LACKS THAT LINE: writes to /api/health are refused by the upstream's 405 rather than by nginx, one layer later than every other path. That is a defence-in-depth gap, not an exposure — the request is still refused and nothing is written — and closing it needs a root edit, because this script deliberately never rewrites a certbot-managed vhost.
